steps.prompt: Both paragraphs start the same story about school lunches. After the first sentence, which one tells you what the paragraph will be about?
steps.a: Lunch happens every day. There are many foods. Some students bring lunch from home.
steps.b: Our school should serve healthier lunches. Right now, the most popular meal is pizza with fries.
steps.reveal: B’s first sentence is a topic sentence: it tells the reader the main idea of the whole paragraph (healthier lunches), so every sentence after it makes sense. A’s first sentence could lead anywhere.

cards.title: What is a topic sentence?
cards.body: A topic sentence states the main idea of a paragraph in one sentence. It usually comes first. Every other sentence in the paragraph supports it.

cards.title: Specific, not vague
cards.showing: Dogs make better pets than cats for busy families.
cards.note: A strong topic sentence takes a position or makes a clear point. Never announce it (“This paragraph is about…”). Just say it.

cards.title: Topic sentence recipe
cards.text:
Topic + what you say about it
School uniforms + save families money → School uniforms save families money.
Recess + should be longer → Recess should be longer for middle schoolers.
cards.note: Not too broad (“Sports are good.”) and not too narrow (“I scored two goals on Saturday.”).

prompts: Which of your topic sentences is the most specific? What makes it specific?
How can a topic sentence help you plan the rest of a paragraph?
